sidebars.body_markdown: A Qualified Institutional Buyer (QIB) is an institution that SEBI considers sophisticated enough to invest without the protections of a public offer. The list includes mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds, foreign portfolio investors, banks, public financial institutions, venture capital funds, and alternative investment funds. Retail investors and high-net-worth individuals are not QIBs. The rationale: QIBs can negotiate terms and assess risk themselves, so the regulator lets companies raise money from them faster, without a full public prospectus.
